- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct — force downward adjustment in next 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply for 5+ days, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast toward historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — reduce initial values by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.3 → +0.6), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
